questions.source: SM LAP 4—Dream Team Maker (Staffing)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: A manager who is developing compensation plans may

options.B: decide where and when training is best conducted.
options.C: extend a job offer with its specific terms and conditions.

questions.explanation: Determine employee eligibility for benefits. A manager who is developing compensation plans may determine employee eligibility for certain benefits. Deciding where and when training is best conducted is part of training and developing. Extending job offers and negotiating with candidates are part of selection.
questions.source: SM LAP 4—Dream Team Maker (Staffing)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: Rhys is a manager who wants to better motivate and communicate with his employees. Which management function should he focus on to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: Directing. The directing management function involves many activities, including motivating employees to achieve goals and communicating with team members. Planning, organizing, and controlling are other management functions that are less involved with motivating and communicating.
questions.source: Thom, R. (2012, August 1). Defining the functions of management. Retrieved January 28, 2016, from http://www.huffingtonpost.com/rayanne-thorn/functions-of-management_b_1723977.html

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss managerial considerations in directing

questions.question: Monica created and implemented a plan for an advertising campaign, and now she wants to know if the plan has been effective in reaching the goals she designed. Which managerial function should she focus on?
questions.explanation: Controlling. Controlling is the management function that monitors the work effort. If Monica is monitoring the effectiveness of her plan and deciding whether or not the company has met its goals, she is focusing on managerial control. This is not part of the planning, directing, or organizing functions of management.
questions.source: Farese, L.S., Kimbrell, G., & Woloszyk, C.A. (2012). Marketing essentials (pp. 257-258). Columbus, OH: Glencoe/McGraw-Hill.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of managerial control (control process, types of control, what is controlled)

questions.question: For successful innovation to occur, employees must be willing to __________ while developing ideas.
questions.explanation: Learn. For successful innovation to occur, employees must be willing to learn while developing ideas. The development process involves learning and accepting change. Employees do not necessarily have to teach while developing ideas. They should review their results and learn from them, not avoid them. Innovation does not necessarily occur when employees work alone; it may happen when employees are working together.
questions.source: Muse, C., & Smith, J. Cultivating innovation in the workplace. Retrieved February 3, 2016, from http://managementhelp.org/innovation/

performanceIndicator.text: Describe relationship among innovation, learning, and change

questions.question: A company is changing over to a new operating system and wants all of its employees to successfully adjust to the change. What can the company do to get all of the employees on board?

options.A: Let the employees know why the change is important after it has occurred.
options.B: Execute the change without telling employees to avoid confusing them.
options.C: Involve only high-ranking employees—lower level employees do not need to be aware of the change.
options.D: Explain to all employees why the change is needed and how it will help.

questions.explanation: Explain to all employees why the change is needed and how it will help. The company should communicate to all employees what the change is and why it is occurring . If employees understand why the change is important and how it will help them, they will have an easier time adjusting to the change. The company should not execute the change without telling employees or only let the employees know about the change after it has occurred. All employees should be involved, not just high-ranking employees.
questions.source: Gilbert, J. (2009, April 14). The change management life cycle; involve your people to ensure success. Retrieved February 2, 2016, from http://www.batimes.com/articles/the-change-management-life-cycle-involve-your-people-to-ensure-success.html

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of change management

questions.question: Many organizational changes fail because

options.A: big changes cannot be executed throughout entire companies.
options.B: companies do not properly execute the change-management lifecycle.
options.C: most people are resistant to change.
options.D: managers give their employees too much time to adjust to changes.

questions.explanation: Companies do not properly execute the change-management lifecycle. Many organizational changes fail because the changes are not implemented properly. Big changes may be difficult to execute throughout entire companies, but it can be done by using the change-management lifecycle. Most people are resistant to change, but executing a change correctly can help them accept the change. Employees may need a large amount of time to adjust to changes.
questions.source: Core, K. (2012, January 20). The basics of change management. Retrieved February 2, 2016, from http://www.examiner.com/article/the-basics-of-change-management

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the change-management lifecycle
